output.headline: Multi-currency rounding keeps going a cent or decimal place wrong

what_keeps_breaking.point: Midpoint amounts were rounded to even instead of half away from zero: 1,234.565 SEK printed as 1,234.56.
Conversion went through double and lost precision, leaving large SEK lines a cent out.
Credit note amounts were truncated rather than rounded like invoice lines, so a full credit of 99.995 left 0.01 open.
Lines were converted without rounding and only the total was rounded, so the printed lines did not add up to the subtotal and the customer's AP rejected the invoice.

Every currency was given two decimal places, so JPY, then KRW and ISK, invoices showed decimals; the fix is a hand-kept list of zero-decimal currencies, and the material does not say whether any other currencies are billed.
VAT was worked out on the unrounded converted amount instead of the rounded line, putting some lines 0.01 SEK out, which touches tax records.

output.why_it_escapes: There are no automated tests for this rule; each fix recorded only a manual case update or nothing, so one-cent and decimal-place regressions in the shared RoundingHelper were seen only when customers' AP systems or banks rejected invoices.

proposed_tests.title: Midpoint line amounts round half away from zero
proposed_tests.scenario: Create a SEK proposal with lines converting to 1,234.565 SEK and 1,234.575 SEK; expect printed lines of 1,234.57 and 1,234.58.

proposed_tests.title: Large conversion is exact in decimal
proposed_tests.scenario: Create a Nordvik (SEK) proposal with a line of 12,345.67 EUR at rate 11.4523; expect the repro's 141,385.32 SEK, though exact decimal multiplication gives 141,386.32, so engineers should confirm the expected figure before encoding it.

proposed_tests.title: Full credit of a converted line clears the invoice
proposed_tests.scenario: On a GBP invoice with a line of 99.995 GBP equivalent, raise a full credit note; expect a credit line of -100.00 and 0.00 left open on the invoice.

proposed_tests.title: Printed lines add up to the subtotal
proposed_tests.scenario: Create a Nordvik (SEK) proposal with 14 time lines of 1.00 EUR at rate 11.4523; expect each line printed as 11.45 SEK and a subtotal of 160.30 SEK (not 160.33), equal to the sum of the printed lines.

proposed_tests.title: Zero-decimal currencies print whole units
proposed_tests.scenario: Create proposals for Kaito Systems (JPY), Hanseo Logistics (KRW) and Fjord Data ehf (ISK) with a line converting to 152,340.47; expect 152,340 with no decimals on lines, tax and totals in each currency, and two decimals for a SEK control proposal.

proposed_tests.title: VAT is worked out on the rounded line
proposed_tests.scenario: Create a SEK proposal with a line of 1.00 EUR at rate 10.015 and VAT at 25.5%; expect line 10.02 SEK, VAT 2.56 SEK (not 2.55) and a total of 12.58 SEK.
